sections.title: Role
sections.text: Damage dealer. This leveling guide is written around a two-handed weapon.

sections.title: Playstyle
sections.text: Fight mainly in Battle Stance. Use Rend and Overpower, manage Rage between pulls, then use Sweeping Strikes to cleave a second target once the talent is available.

sections.title: Strengths
items: Strong damage against two nearby enemies with Sweeping Strikes.
Overpower can deal efficient damage for little Rage.
Weaponmaster supports multiple main weapon types without a respec.
Strong opening damage when entering a fight with Rage already pooled.

sections.title: Weaknesses
items: Limited self-healing can increase downtime between pulls.
Slow weapon swings make missed attacks costly.
Bleed-immune enemies reduce the value of Rend and Bloodthrill.
Changing targets can waste Overpower opportunities.

equipmentGuide.weaponAdvice: Compare current weapon DPS first. When weapon DPS is similar, the guide prefers a slower swing; it cautions against passing a large DPS upgrade for speed or weapon type.
equipmentGuide.importantAttributes: Compare weapon damage, DPS, speed and the listed Strength, Stamina or Attack Power. No level-by-level stat weights are recorded here.
equipmentGuide.armorAdvice: The recorded leveling milestone lists Plate Armor training at level 40. No verified level-specific armor item list is recorded.
equipmentGuide.survivabilityAdvice: Choose armor your character can currently wear and compare its defensive attributes; this guide does not record a sourced armor upgrade path.
equipmentGuide.upgradeRationale: The Arms leveling guide emphasizes weapon upgrades. A listed item is only a candidate: compare its damage, DPS, speed and attributes with your equipped weapon before replacing it.

sections.title: Recommendation label
sections.text: These are the cited guide’s profession recommendations and crafting pairings, not required Warrior mechanics.

attributes.name: Strength
attributes.summary: Each point gives 2 melee Attack Power; every 20 Strength also gives 1 Block Value for Warriors.
attributes.when: Useful throughout leveling and at 60: it raises weapon damage and ability damage. For Protection, it also contributes Block Value.

attributes.name: Agility
attributes.summary: At level 60, 20 Agility gives 1% melee crit; each point adds 2 Armor and some Dodge. Warriors gain no melee Attack Power from it.
attributes.when: Compare it with Strength on gear; it is especially useful to Protection because it adds Armor and Dodge as well as crit. The crit conversion varies by level.

attributes.name: Stamina
attributes.summary: The first 20 points each give 1 health; each additional point gives 10 health before buffs. It supports survival, especially for tanks.
attributes.when: More valuable when pulls or dungeon hits threaten to kill you; it protects against both physical and magic damage.

attributes.name: Attack Power
attributes.summary: Every 14 Attack Power adds 1 weapon DPS before modifiers; it also improves abilities that scale with Attack Power.
attributes.when: A useful offensive stat at every level, but compare it with direct weapon upgrades and Strength rather than treating it as a cap target.

attributes.name: Critical Strike
attributes.summary: Increases the chance attacks crit. Critical auto-attacks generate more Rage; Fury also uses crits to trigger Flurry.
attributes.when: Useful for damage and auto-attack Rage; for Fury it gains extra value from Flurry after the recommended build reaches level 37.

attributes.name: Hit Chance
attributes.summary: Reduces attack misses. Missed auto-attacks deal no damage and generate no Rage.
attributes.when: Take it when gear offers it without giving up a major weapon or role stat. Boss-target numbers apply only to the stated level-60 encounter, not while leveling.

attributes.name: Weapon Damage
attributes.summary: Weapon DPS and per-swing damage affect attacks differently; compare the whole weapon and its stats.
attributes.when: Important throughout leveling and at 60. Arms values per-swing damage with its two-hander; Fury must keep both weapons current; Protection's key abilities do not all scale with weapon damage.

attributes.name: Expertise
attributes.summary: Reduces enemy dodges and parries. It addresses a different miss result from Hit Chance.
attributes.when: Useful when available on gear. It supports reliable attacks and Protection threat; the cited dodge reference is for attacking level-63 bosses from behind.

attributes.name: Defense
attributes.summary: Above the level-based baseline, Defense improves Dodge, Parry and Block while reducing enemy Hit and Critical Strike chance.
attributes.when: Mostly a Protection dungeon or raid survival stat. The 440 Defense figure is a level-60 raid-boss critical-immunity reference, not a leveling target.

attributes.name: Armor
attributes.summary: Reduces incoming physical damage; it does not reduce magic damage.
attributes.when: Most useful when Protection is tanking physical attackers; Stamina covers health needs against both physical and magic damage.

attributes.name: Block Value
attributes.summary: Reduces damage when blocking and improves Shield Slam damage.
attributes.when: Protection values it with a shield. Its offensive value grows when Shield Slam is learned at level 40; block-value scaling is not an Arms or Fury priority.

explanations.title: Hit, Expertise and target level
explanations.text: For level-60 PvE against level-63 raid bosses, the cited guides use 8% Hit for special attacks and two-handed attacks. Dual-wield auto-attacks can continue to miss beyond that point. Expertise reduces dodges and parries rather than misses; 6.5% dodge reduction is the cited behind-target reference for level-63 bosses. These are not universal leveling caps.

explanations.title: Weapon damage, speed and Rage
explanations.text: Weapon DPS describes average damage over time; damage per swing affects weapon-based attacks such as Mortal Strike. At similar DPS, a slower weapon hits harder per swing, but speed alone is not a reason to reject a clear DPS upgrade. In Forever, normal-swing Rage depends on weapon speed, not damage dealt.

explanations.title: Tank survival: Armor, Defense and Block
explanations.text: Armor reduces physical damage. Defense improves avoidance and blocking while reducing incoming hit and crit chance; the Forever reference lists 440 total Defense for raid-boss critical immunity, while the Protection guide explains Shield Block can temporarily fill the combat table. Block Value reduces blocked damage and contributes to Shield Slam.

statsGuide.upgradeAdvice: Compare a weapon upgrade using its DPS, per-swing damage and other stats together. A clearly stronger weapon is usually more meaningful than a small secondary-stat gain; at similar DPS, weapon speed can matter to weapon-damage attacks. For other slots, use the selected role’s guide order and consider survival needs. No stat weights are stored here.

starterGuide.resource: Mana can run low during repeated ability use; use the pet and basic attacks to avoid needless casts.

starterGuide.gear: Keep your ranged weapon current; the guide recommends an early bow upgrade.

A critical hit can pull threat from your pet; use defensive tools and bring a loose enemy toward the group tank.

classes.name: Priest
classes.description: A cloth-wearing spellcaster who supports allies with healing and buffs or turns to damaging magic.
strengths: Supports allies through buffs and healing.
Holy and Discipline include healing tools; Shadow provides a damage path.
limitations: Wears cloth armor and has few ways to escape enemies.
soloTips: Limited escape tools make positioning and avoiding unwanted enemies useful considerations.
groupUtility: Healing and buffs strengthen party members.

starterGuide.reason: The Forever guide recommends wand damage and Spirit Tap to limit Mana downtime, with shield and healing spells as safety tools.
combat: Use a small number of spells, then finish with your wand to conserve Mana.
Power Word: Shield can reduce incoming damage and spell pushback when solo.
starterGuide.resource: Mana is tight early; a current wand is a major upgrade, and Spirit Tap rewards a killing blow.
starterGuide.classMilestones: The guide lists race-specific Priest quests; consult the class quest route for the player’s race.
starterGuide.gear: Upgrade your wand regularly; the source says wand auto-attacks make a large share of early damage.
beginnerMistakes: Repeatedly casting every damage spell on every mob creates unnecessary Mana downtime.
Priest is less tanky and mobile than many classes; avoid extra pulls.
starterGuide.zoneAdvice: Use the linked guide’s level slider for faction-specific zone brackets and quest rewards.

journeySteps.label: Level 10: check the race-specific Priest quest route.
Level 20: check the second race-specific Priest quest route.

levelingBands.combat: A good wand matters: use a few spells, then let the wand finish the enemy to protect Mana.
levelingBands.survival: Power Word: Shield helps prevent damage and spell pushback.
levelingBands.milestones: Wand Specialization and Spirit Tap are the guide’s early talent priorities.

levelingBands.combat: Continue the wand-and-Mana rhythm; check your race-specific Priest class quest at level 10.
levelingBands.survival: Use the shield when solo enemies can interrupt your casts.
levelingBands.milestones: Race-specific Priest quest at 10; Inner Fire at 12.

levelingBands.combat: Mind Flay and Devouring Plague are listed at 20; Vampiric Embrace is a talent milestone at 25.
levelingBands.survival: The guide recommends spending only the Mana needed, then finishing with your wand.
levelingBands.milestones: Mind Flay and Devouring Plague 20; Vampiric Embrace talent 25.

classes.name: Shaman
classes.description: An adaptable elemental combatant whose totems provide buffs, healing and utility.
strengths: Can deal melee or spell damage and heal.
Mail armor and shields contribute to its sturdier class toolkit.
limitations: The official overview describes limited crowd control.
groupUtility: Totems provide buffs, healing and utility.
Can fill damage or healing roles.

starterGuide.reason: A melee path with strong burst, self-healing and Ghost Wolf mobility; its key limitation is early Mana pressure.
combat: Before level 30, use Rockbiter Weapon; apply Lightning Shield between pulls.
At level 25, Stormstrike is a major milestone; use it when ready and spend shocks deliberately.
starterGuide.resource: Auto-attacks can finish weak enemies without Mana. Spirit regeneration pauses for five seconds after spending Mana.
starterGuide.classMilestones: Call of Fire should be completed promptly for the Fire Totem; Call of Water opens at 20. Other totem quests take travel, and Call of Air requires a Razorfen Kraul run.
starterGuide.gear: Keep a slow two-handed weapon current; the guide prioritizes weapon DPS, then values Intellect for damage scaling and Mana.
beginnerMistakes: Overcasting slows your pace through drinking.
Multiple enemies can overwhelm you; use self-healing and utility rather than assuming every pull is safe.
starterGuide.zoneAdvice: The source lists Alliance early routes through Loch Modan, Westfall and Darkshore; Horde through The Barrens and Silverpine. Use its live level-sensitive route.

journeySteps.label: Call of Earth: level 4 details in the source are for Dwarf Shamans; other race routes differ.
Call of Fire: pick up the Shaman quest for your Fire Totem.
Call of Water: the Water Totem quest opens at level 20.
Call of Air: the route includes a Razorfen Kraul run; exact level varies by race route.

levelingBands.combat: Use Rockbiter Weapon before level 30, keep Lightning Shield up between pulls, and let auto-attacks finish weak enemies.
levelingBands.survival: Call of Earth level-4 details in the source are specific to Dwarf Shamans.
levelingBands.milestones: Call of Earth quest route varies by race.

levelingBands.combat: Pick up Call of Fire for the Fire Totem; drop useful totems before engaging rather than spending Mana mid-fight without a reason.
levelingBands.survival: Mana is the early constraint; spending Mana pauses Spirit regeneration for five seconds.
levelingBands.milestones: Call of Fire quest; Shamanistic Focus is recommended at 20.

levelingBands.combat: Call of Water opens at 20. Stormstrike is a key level-25 build milestone; Windfury Weapon becomes available at 30.
levelingBands.survival: Use Shocks selectively and keep your weapon upgraded.
levelingBands.milestones: Shamanistic Focus 20; Stormstrike around 25; Windfury Weapon 30.

classes.name: Mage
classes.description: A fragile ranged spellcaster who chooses among Arcane, Fire and Frost tools.
strengths: Offers ranged single-target and area damage.
Polymorph provides crowd control.
Can provide party buffs and conjured food and water.
limitations: Fragile when caught in melee combat.
soloTips: Frost offers combat control; the official overview does not rank a leveling build.
groupUtility: Polymorph, party buffs, and conjured food and water.

starterGuide.reason: Forever’s Arcane tree is reworked around Arcane Blast and Missile Barrage, making it a supported leveling option rather than a generic Classic-era fallback.
combat: Build damage with Arcane Blast and use Arcane Missiles when Missile Barrage procs.
Use crowd control and range to prevent enemies from interrupting casts.
starterGuide.resource: Arcane talents improve Mana efficiency, but spell-heavy pulls still require watching your Mana and using conjured supplies.
starterGuide.classMilestones: The linked Forever guide has level-based class milestones; no separate quest unlock is asserted here.
starterGuide.gear: The source recommends keeping crafting gear in mind; specific stat priorities should follow the current guide.
beginnerMistakes: Standing still to cast can be risky when enemies reach you.
Do not apply Retail or old Classic rotations to Forever’s Arcane changes.
starterGuide.zoneAdvice: The source provides level-sensitive zone and dungeon suggestions; choose the current faction and level there.

journeySteps.label: Level 20: Arcane Blast becomes available in the Forever Arcane leveling guide.
Level 25: Missile Barrage is a listed Arcane milestone.

levelingBands.combat: Play at range and avoid pulling more enemies than you can safely cast through. The Forever guide identifies Arcane as a redesigned leveling option.
levelingBands.survival: Arcane is a caster path; bad proc luck or gear can increase downtime.
levelingBands.milestones: No exact talent allocation is recorded for this band.

levelingBands.combat: Use the spells you have trained and conserve Mana between pulls; do not import a Retail or other Classic rotation.
levelingBands.survival: Arcane’s Forever changes make its own leveling guide the relevant reference.
levelingBands.milestones: No exact talent milestone recorded before the new Arcane core.

levelingBands.combat: Arcane Blast is listed at 20 and Missile Barrage at 25; use Arcane Missiles when the proc empowers it.
levelingBands.survival: Arcane’s resource talents help sustain, but watch Mana during repeated casts.
levelingBands.milestones: Arcane Blast 20; Missile Barrage 25; Arcane Explosion 14.

classes.name: Warlock
classes.description: A spellcaster who combines Shadow and Fire magic with demonic allies.
strengths: Forever specializations support damage-over-time, demon synergies, and Shadow/Fire combinations.
Pets scale with their master’s stats.
limitations: Physically weak and relies on demon pets for protection.
soloTips: Demon pets can help protect the Warlock; no comparative leveling ranking is published here.

starterGuide.reason: A damage-over-time playstyle with a demon, drains and Life Tap; the Forever guide emphasizes planning health and Mana together.
combat: Use your demon deliberately: Voidwalker offers safer solo pulls; keep pet commands easy to reach.
Apply damage-over-time spells, then use direct damage or drains as the situation allows.
starterGuide.resource: Life Tap converts health into Mana; use Drain Life, food and bandages to manage the health cost.
starterGuide.classMilestones: Warlock class quests involve travel and demon unlocks; pick up the chain before leaving town and consult the class quest guide for exact race/level steps.
starterGuide.gear: The leveling guide values Spell Power and Shadow damage for its main spells; choose current upgrades rather than a fixed item list.
beginnerMistakes: Life Tap at low health can leave you vulnerable.
Keep demon Grimoires trained; pet ability ranks are handled separately.
starterGuide.zoneAdvice: Collect flight paths and combine class-quest travel with nearby zone and trainer stops.

journeySteps.label: Level 6: train Life Tap; balance its health cost with recovery.
Level 20: Rain of Fire adds a ranged area-damage option.

levelingBands.combat: Life Tap is learned at 6; trade health for Mana carefully and use Drain Life or recovery between fights.
levelingBands.survival: Keep an eye on Health before using Life Tap again.
levelingBands.milestones: Life Tap 6; Immolate is available from level 1.

levelingBands.combat: Use your demon and damage-over-time spells to manage pressure; train spell ranks and demon abilities at trainers.
levelingBands.survival: Use Life Tap with recovery in mind, not as free Mana.
levelingBands.milestones: Drain Life 14; guide lists Corruption ranks beginning at 4 and Shadow Bolt ranks at 1.

levelingBands.combat: Rain of Fire is listed at 20; Shadow Bolt can gain instant-cast Nightfall procs from 25 in the guide’s build.
levelingBands.survival: Area casts can spend resources quickly; avoid adding enemies just because an AoE spell is available.
levelingBands.milestones: Rain of Fire 20; Nightfall talent procs from 25; Firestone is listed from 28.

classes.name: Druid
classes.description: A nature-focused class with adaptable forms and distinct spellcasting, melee and healing paths.
strengths: Feral supports form-based melee and tanking approaches.
Balance provides a spellcasting damage path.
Restoration focuses on healing.
groupUtility: Can approach combat through damage, tanking or healing paths.

starterGuide.reason: The Forever guide highlights Feral’s flexibility between damage and tanking, mobility and self-healing. Bear and Cat forms arrive at levels 10 and 20.
combat: Use the form suited to the task: Bear for durability, Cat for melee damage once available.
Expect a slower opening before the form unlocks; use healing tools between fights.
starterGuide.resource: Shifting and healing have costs; avoid unnecessary form changes and keep recovery between pulls in mind.
starterGuide.classMilestones: Form unlocks are major class milestones; the linked class-quest guide has race-specific quest steps.
starterGuide.gear: Follow the source’s level-sensitive priorities; no single weapon/stat rule is assumed for all forms.
beginnerMistakes: Feral’s full leveling rhythm changes at levels 10 and 20 as forms unlock.
Do not treat Bear and Cat as identical roles.
starterGuide.zoneAdvice: Use the source’s live faction and level route; the linked guide includes Forever-specific dungeon and zone recommendations.

levelingBands.combat: Feral’s leveling pace improves after its forms unlock; use the class kit and avoid assuming the later Cat/Bear rhythm is already available.
levelingBands.survival: The guide calls the pre-form stretch slower than later leveling.
levelingBands.milestones: No exact talent allocation recorded for this band.

levelingBands.combat: Bear Form becomes available at 10, adding the path’s tank-oriented form option.
levelingBands.survival: Use the form that fits the pull rather than treating every fight as Cat play.
levelingBands.milestones: Bear Form level 10.

levelingBands.combat: Cat Form becomes available at 20; the Forever guide highlights Feral’s mobility and ability to shift between damage and tank roles.
levelingBands.survival: The guide notes Cat Form has no AoE damage.
levelingBands.milestones: Cat Form level 20.

shamanGuide.classMechanics: Shaman uses Mana and places stationary totems for elemental buffs and utility. Totems can support damage, defense, movement control or group recovery; moving between pulls may mean placing them again. Mana spent on spells or totems can create downtime, so spend it with intent.

arms.text: For solo questing, use a two-handed weapon and compare upgrades by damage per second; train the new weapon skill after swapping. Keep Rage for high-priority attacks instead of spending it all on Heroic Strike.

fury.text: Before level 20, use your strongest weapon; a good two-hander works well. At level 20, train Dual Wield and maintain both weapon skills. Fury’s damage improves substantially with Whirlwind at 36, so conserve Rage and keep both weapons current as you level.

protection.text: Use a one-handed weapon and shield. Revenge becomes available at 14 and Protection is slower before Shield Block at 16; after that, defensive blocks can support both survival and Revenge use. This setup also prepares you to tank dungeons when your group needs a tank.

arms.title: Improved Overpower talent
arms.text: Take both Improved Overpower points at levels 15–16; the cited Arms guide says the added critical-strike chance makes Overpower a strong, low-Rage response to Dodge procs.

arms.title: Spearing Strike talent
arms.text: The cited Arms build takes Spearing Strike at 25. Use it when Rage allows, especially against Giants, Dragonkin, and mounted targets; the guide reports bonus damage against those types and a dismount effect.

arms.title: Recklessness
arms.text: The Arms leveling guide lists Recklessness as a level-50 ability unlock.

arms.title: Reckless Swings
arms.text: The Arms guide lists Reckless Swings at 56 for its build. It costs health to generate extra Rage on the next attacks, so use it when you can keep attacking and have health to spare.

arms.title: Sweeping Strikes talent
arms.text: The recommended Arms build adds Sweeping Strikes at level 30, improving fights against two nearby enemies.

arms.title: Mortal Strike
arms.text: The recommended Arms build learns Mortal Strike at 40; preserve Rage for it while keeping Rend and Overpower relevant.

fury.title: Gore Drinker talent
fury.text: The recommended Fury build takes Gore Drinker at levels 32–33 to improve sustain while attacking.

fury.title: Whirlwind
fury.text: Whirlwind becomes Fury’s main attack in the cited leveling guide; it requires Berserker Stance.

fury.title: Flurry talent
fury.text: The recommended build reaches Flurry at level 37; keep both weapon skills current to benefit from the faster attacks.

fury.title: Bloodthirst
fury.text: The recommended Fury build learns Bloodthirst at 40 and uses it while Whirlwind is on cooldown, keeping Rage for the next Whirlwind.

fury.title: Improved Berserker Rage talent
fury.text: The cited Fury build takes this talent at levels 41–42. With both points, Berserker Rage generates Rage immediately and removes movement-impairing effects.

fury.title: Deflection talent
fury.text: The cited Fury build spends levels 43–47 on Deflection for additional Parry chance while questing.

fury.title: Improved Charge talent
fury.text: The cited Fury build takes Improved Charge at levels 48–49. Continue to account for Rage loss when switching stances.

fury.title: Recklessness
fury.text: The Fury leveling guide lists Recklessness as a level-50 ability unlock.

fury.title: Improved Tactical Mastery talent
fury.text: Take this talent at levels 50–52 in the cited build. With Tactical Mastery, it raises the Rage retained across stance changes to 25; excess Rage is still lost.

fury.title: Anger Management talent
fury.text: The cited build takes Anger Management at level 53 as part of its late-level Rage management path.

fury.title: Improved Bloodrage talent
fury.text: The cited Fury build takes Improved Bloodrage at levels 54–55 to gain more Rage from Bloodrage.

fury.title: Enrage talent
fury.text: The cited build invests in Enrage from levels 56–60. Incoming damage can activate it, increasing physical damage and adding another way to build Gore Drinker stacks.

protection.title: Revenge
protection.text: Revenge is the core early Protection attack in the cited build; keep enemies in front and use Shield Block after it becomes available to help trigger it.

protection.title: Shield Block
protection.text: Shield Block improves survival against blockable melee attacks and supports Revenge opportunities.

protection.title: Vanguard talent
protection.text: The recommended build takes Vanguard at level 25, allowing Charge from Defensive Stance; this is a build milestone, not a universal talent requirement.

protection.title: Shield Slam
protection.text: The recommended Protection build learns Shield Slam at level 40; shield Block Value also contributes to its damage.

protection.title: Recklessness
protection.text: The Protection leveling guide lists Recklessness as a level-50 ability milestone.

protection.title: Reckless Swings
protection.text: This build takes Reckless Swings at level 59. It spends health to generate extra Rage from the next four melee attacks; use it only when you have health to spare and can keep attacking.

preparationTips.text: Before changing zones, compare the next zone’s verified level range with your level and finish remaining quests that still fit. Train available abilities, check weapon skill after changing weapon type, and check equipment durability. Before a dungeon, collect its available quests. These are general preparation checks, not verified zone-specific quest routes.

elemental.title: Elemental · spell damage and Mana pacing
elemental.text: Use range to start fights on your terms. Spend Mana deliberately, avoid chaining costly casts when a melee follow-up is safe, and pause between pulls when needed. Treat the leveling guide's spell and talent unlocks as milestones; no complete Elemental zone-by-zone build is recorded here.

enhancement.title: Enhancement · two-handed melee progression
enhancement.text: The Forever leveling guide recommends a slow two-handed weapon, Rockbiter before level 30 and Windfury Weapon from 30. Stormstrike is a level-25 talent milestone; keep a current weapon and use shocks selectively to limit Mana downtime.

restoration.title: Restoration · group healing and slower solo play
restoration.text: The Forever guide advises against solo leveling as Restoration and recommends group play or dungeon healing. Healing Wave is the basic single-target heal; use Mana-efficient spells and pause casting when the group is safe so Mana can regenerate.

preparationTips.text: Train class abilities at a Shaman trainer as they unlock. Totem quests have their own minimum levels and must be completed manually; reaching the level does not award or complete a totem quest. The Water quest has long cross-zone travel, and the Air quest's weapon follow-up is substantially harder than the totem handoff.

totems.name: Stoneskin Totem
totems.use: Choose for party-wide physical mitigation when incoming melee damage matters.
totems.alternative: Use Strength of Earth when the group benefits more from its Strength buff, or Earthbind when controlling nearby movement matters.

totems.name: Stoneclaw Totem
totems.use: Distract nearby fresh enemies briefly when a pull needs to be separated or you need space to retreat.
totems.alternative: Earthbind slows pursuers; Stoneskin is better when group mitigation matters.

totems.name: Earthbind Totem
totems.use: Slow nearby enemies when creating room to cast, heal, or retreat.
totems.alternative: Choose Stoneskin or Strength of Earth when party mitigation or damage support is more useful than movement control.

totems.name: Strength of Earth Totem
totems.use: Buff nearby party members when Strength improves their melee output.
totems.alternative: Use Stoneskin against physical pressure or Earthbind for control; only one Earth totem can occupy the element slot at a time.

totems.name: Tremor Totem
totems.use: Drop when nearby party members need Fear, Charm, or Sleep effects removed.
totems.alternative: Use a mitigation or damage Earth totem when no listed crowd-control effect needs cleansing.

totems.name: Searing Totem
totems.use: Place before a longer single-target fight so its repeated attacks can repay the Mana spent.
totems.alternative: Prefer Magma Totem for nearby groups; skip a Fire totem when a short fight or unwanted extra aggro makes its cost poor value.

totems.name: Flametongue Totem
totems.use: Support a melee-heavy party with its main-hand weapon effect when its output fits the group.
totems.alternative: Choose Searing or Magma for direct Fire damage when a group weapon buff is not useful.

totems.name: Fire Resistance Totem
totems.use: Use when party members are taking meaningful Fire spell damage.
totems.alternative: Prefer a Fire damage totem when Fire resistance has no encounter value.

totems.name: Magma Totem
totems.use: Use for sustained nearby area damage when enemies will remain close to the totem.
totems.alternative: Searing Totem is the lower-cost single-target choice; conserve Mana if enemies will die quickly.

totems.name: Healing Stream Totem
totems.use: Add steady nearby group healing when party members can remain within its range.
totems.alternative: Use Mana Spring for a group with greater Mana pressure, or a direct heal when one ally needs immediate recovery.

totems.name: Mana Spring Totem
totems.use: Support nearby Mana users during longer group fights.
totems.alternative: Healing Stream is preferable when party health is the more immediate concern; avoid spending Mana on it for a nearly finished pull.

totems.name: Mana Tide Totem
totems.use: Use during a longer group fight after allies have spent enough Mana to benefit from its restoration.
totems.alternative: Mana Spring is the trainer-learned Water totem for ongoing regeneration when Mana Tide is not talented or is on cooldown.

totems.name: Poison Cleansing Totem
totems.use: Use when party members are affected by removable poison within the totem's range.
totems.alternative: Use Healing Stream or Mana Spring when no poison needs removal.

totems.name: Windfury Totem
totems.use: Support nearby melee attackers in a group; Forever allows this totem to coexist with a Shaman weapon imbue.
totems.alternative: Grace of Air is another group offensive option after level 42; choose based on the party and encounter.

totems.name: Grounding Totem
totems.use: Use when an incoming hostile spell can be intercepted by the totem.
totems.alternative: Prefer Windfury or Grace of Air for a group damage buff when spell interception is not needed.

totems.name: Grace of Air Totem
totems.use: Buff nearby party members when its Agility benefit fits the group.
totems.alternative: Use Windfury for a melee group when its extra attacks are preferable; only one Air totem can be active at a time.

singleTarget.when: Main ranged damage spell; cast from range and avoid starting a cast that will finish after a target is nearly dead.
Apply to a target that will live long enough for its damage over time to matter.

Use against multiple targets when its cost and threat are acceptable; it unlocks at level 32.

Heal between casts or when survival requires it; do not trade a necessary heal for damage.
Slow pursuers to regain casting space or retreat.

opening.when: Refresh between pulls so the buff does not consume combat time.
If its quest is complete, place before a longer single-target pull.

elemental.resource: Mana is the limiting resource. Spend a final buff or totem after the last damaging cast when practical so the five-second Spirit regeneration delay begins sooner; finish weak targets with a weapon swing rather than an unnecessary spell.
elemental.extraAdvice: Stay at range and stop a cast if an enemy is about to interrupt it. Earth Shock is the Shaman interrupt; use it for dangerous casts, not as a routine damage button.

singleTarget.when: Use when the selected recommended talent route has allocated it; its Forever tooltip unlock timing has conflicting reports, so the local conservative build does not allocate it before level 43.
Use selectively for an interrupt or when burst damage is worth the Mana.
Use to pull from range; if Maelstrom Weapon is talented, cast after building its full stack.

multipleEnemies.when: Use around an active Fire Totem when targets are close and the Mana cost is worthwhile.
At level 32+, use on multiple targets when the Mana and threat cost fits the pull.
Use only for groups that will stay near it long enough to justify its high Mana cost.

defensive.when: Recover between pulls or make a deliberate emergency heal.
Use as a short defensive distraction when a dangerous pull needs control.
Use to disengage or travel; it prevents attacking while active.

opening.when: Use as the economical solo imbue before level 30.
Use from level 30 for the current Enhancement leveling recommendation; reapply between fights rather than spending combat time.
Apply between pulls.

enhancement.resource: Auto-attacks cost no Mana and are a useful way to finish weak targets. Shocks, heals, and totems all compete for Mana; choose only the casts that change the fight. Spirit regeneration pauses for five seconds after Mana expenditure.
enhancement.extraAdvice: Keep a current, slow two-handed weapon. Forever does not use the Classic dual-wield leveling setup; Windfury Weapon and Windfury Totem can coexist under current Forever rules.

singleTarget.when: If allocated by the selected Restoration talent route, use on a hurt target; the Forever talent also empowers your next Chain Heal on that target.
Use for measured single-target healing; choose a lower rank when it fully covers the damage.
Use when a faster cast is more valuable than Healing Wave efficiency, especially under pressure.

multipleEnemies.when: Apply to an injured party member before Chain Heal when its talent is available.
At level 40 and above, use on an injured target when multiple nearby allies need healing; choose a lower rank if it is sufficient.
Use for focused damage when group healing is not needed.

defensive.when: If allocated, pair with a high-value emergency Nature heal when a cast would be too slow.
Use for urgent single-target recovery when its faster cast matters.
Interrupt a dangerous cast if the party can spare your Mana and global cooldown.

opening.when: After completing Call of Water, set up group healing before combat when the group will remain nearby.
Use for longer group fights with Mana users when healing is not the more urgent Water totem need.

restoration.resource: Mana is the main healing limit. Down-rank Healing Wave when it covers the damage, use Chain Heal only when several allies can benefit, and leave time between casts for Spirit regeneration. Mana Tide Totem is a talent and only appears as available when the selected automatic build allocates it.
restoration.extraAdvice: Restoration is a group-healing specialization and has weaker solo damage support. For solo questing, use Lightning Bolt to pull, let weapon attacks finish low-health enemies, and heal between fights; do not assume a healer damage rotation.

warriorCombat.description: Leveling fundamentals and situational priority lists. These are priorities, not fixed rotations.

opening.when: Open with this before combat when the area is safe; it builds Rage and starts you in melee.
Apply early only if the target will live through most of the bleed.
React to an enemy Dodge or a verified proc and use the opportunity before it expires.
At level 40 and above, keep Rage available for this high-priority attack.

singleTarget.when: Keep the group buff active; refresh when needed and Rage permits.
Apply if the enemy will survive most of its duration; do not refresh on a nearly defeated target.
Use on a Dodge or eligible proc before the opportunity expires; it is a key Arms attack.
From its verified unlock, use when you have surplus Rage after higher-priority attacks; before the Improved Slam talent, time it after an auto attack.
From level 40, use when ready while preserving Rage for Rend, Overpower, and an interrupt.
Spend spare Rage on durable targets; stack mainly on elites and bosses.
Use only with excess Rage because it replaces an auto attack that would generate Rage.

multipleEnemies.when: From level 30, pool Rage and use against two nearby targets so attacks also hit the second enemy.
Use as a Rage dump only after preserving Rage for main attacks; focus one enemy to reduce incoming damage.
Keep it on targets likely to live through most of the bleed, especially when enabling Arms proc talents.
Use eligible procs before they expire and on the target that triggered the opportunity.
From its verified unlock, stance requirements apply; use when several nearby enemies make it worthwhile.

defensive.when: Use for an emergency reduction in incoming damage or to take an enemy off an ally; stance changes can discard excess Rage.
Use early against melee enemies when reducing their damage will help you stay in the fight.
Use against a dangerous weapon-wielding enemy when its effect is useful.
Switch to the required stance and interrupt a dangerous cast when the opportunity warrants the Rage and stance change.
Reserve for a dangerous burst of incoming damage.

arms.rageManagement: Rage comes from attacks, incoming damage, Charge, and Bloodrage. Missed swings generate none; critical auto attacks generate more. Keep enough Rage for Overpower, Mortal Strike once learned, and interrupts. Heroic Strike and Cleave replace an auto attack and its Rage generation, so spend on them only when Rage is excessive. Carry Rage into the next pull when practical.

opening.when: Open with Charge when the area is safe. Before Whirlwind is learned, use Battle Stance; later the source recommends switching to Berserker Stance before reaching the target.
Before Whirlwind is available, apply only when the target will survive most of the bleed.
From level 36, use as the main attack while remaining in Berserker Stance.
From level 40, use between Whirlwind casts and retain Rage for the next Whirlwind.

singleTarget.when: Keep the group buff active; use Bloodrage to prepare Rage or prevent decay, spaced between other Rage and healing effects.
Open when safe; stance guidance changes after Berserker Stance and Whirlwind become available.
Before level 36, apply if the enemy will survive the bleed; stop using it once Whirlwind is learned.
Before level 36, use on a Dodge proc when low on Rage and before it expires.
From level 36, prioritize this main attack and stay in Berserker Stance.
From level 40, use while Whirlwind is on cooldown and preserve Rage for the next Whirlwind.
Use as a finisher below its verified health threshold when spending Rage will secure the kill.
Use only with excess Rage after preserving enough for main attacks and interrupts.

multipleEnemies.when: From level 36, use against nearby enemies and keep the required Berserker Stance.
Use for a second nearby enemy only when Rage remains after higher-priority attacks.
Use between Whirlwind casts from level 40; avoid delaying the next Whirlwind.
Maintain the party buff and avoid spreading damage so widely that enemies stay alive longer.

defensive.when: Use for an emergency defensive or to taunt an enemy from an ally; return to your damage stance when safe.
From its unlock, use to break or prevent Fear and Incapacitate effects; avoid wasting it before a likely control effect.
Use from the required stance to interrupt a dangerous cast.
Use against dangerous weapon-wielding enemies when it can reduce pressure.
Reserve for a dangerous burst of incoming damage.

fury.rageManagement: Rage comes from auto attacks, incoming damage, Charge, and Bloodrage; Fury talents can add Rage from weapon attacks. Misses generate none, and critical auto attacks generate more. Pool enough for Whirlwind and Bloodthirst once learned. Space Rage-generating abilities rather than activating all together when Gore Drinker healing stacks are relevant. Heroic Strike and Cleave replace a Rage-generating auto attack, so reserve them for excess Rage.

opening.when: When safe, Charge before combat. Until the source-listed Vanguard talent at level 25, use Battle Stance for Charge and then switch to Defensive Stance.
Use as your main stance after opening; it improves mitigation and threat, and enables core tank abilities.
Apply early if the target will survive most of the bleed.
Use against melee attacks to mitigate hits and help make Revenge available.
Use when a Block, Dodge, or Parry makes it available; it is an efficient core attack.

singleTarget.when: Keep the group buff active when Rage allows; use Bloodrage between pulls to build Rage and limit decay.
From level 40, prioritize when Rage allows; if Rage is low, use Revenge first.
Use whenever available after a Block, Dodge, or Parry; keep enemies in front so defensive reactions can occur.
Use against melee attacks to reduce damage and help activate Revenge; it is not useful against attacks that cannot be blocked.
Apply early only if the target will survive most of the bleed.
Spend extra Rage on long-lived targets; build five stacks mainly on bosses.
Use only with excessive Rage after reserving enough for Shield Slam, Revenge, or an interrupt.

multipleEnemies.when: Use early to reduce incoming physical pressure from a pack.
Use to damage and slow nearby enemies; maintain threat on targets outside its target cap.
Use against melee attackers to mitigate and help activate Revenge.
Use when available and Rage permits, then switch targets as needed to spread dungeon threat.
Use after a Block, Dodge, or Parry and rotate targets to build threat across a dungeon pack.
Spend excess Rage on a second nearby enemy after preserving resources for core tank abilities.

defensive.when: Remain here as your main tank stance for mitigation, threat, Taunt, and core Protection abilities.
Use against blockable melee attacks when mitigation or an opportunity to trigger Revenge matters.
Reduce incoming physical damage from nearby enemies when useful.
Use on a specific enemy that has stopped attacking you, then build threat before switching targets.
Use against especially dangerous weapon-wielding enemies.
Switch to the required stance and interrupt a dangerous cast when the stance and Rage tradeoff is worthwhile.
Reserve for a dangerous burst of incoming damage.

protection.rageManagement: Rage comes from auto attacks, incoming damage, Charge, and Bloodrage. Protection also gains Rage through blocks and defensive reactions supported by its talents. Auto attack Rage is normalized; missed attacks generate none and critical auto attacks generate more. Save enough for Shield Slam and Revenge, especially while tanking. Heroic Strike and Cleave replace Rage-generating auto attacks, so use them only after your main threat and survival needs are covered.

warriorProfessions.recommendationDisclosure: These are practical profession fits, not requirements or a universal best choice. Specialization notes apply general Warrior play to verified profession benefits; no exclusive specialization profession bonus is recorded.

arms.title: Arms · weapon progression
arms.text: Mining + Blacksmithing is a sourced Warrior leveling option: ore supports weapon and armor crafts, and Blacksmithing weapon stones support weapon damage. Compare each craft with the weapon you already have; the Heavy Copper Maul below is one recorded early option.

fury.title: Fury · damage and supplies
fury.text: Mining + Blacksmithing remains a sourced Warrior option for weapon crafts and weapon stones. Herbalism + Alchemy is another verified gathering/crafting pairing for potions and other consumables; the source data does not establish a Fury-only recipe or profession bonus.

protection.title: Protection · armor and preparation
protection.text: Blacksmithing can craft weapons and mail or plate armor, with Mining supplying ore and stone. This is a practical fit for checking armor upgrades while leveling; no Protection-only recipe or survivability bonus from primary professions is verified here.

combinations.name: Mining + Blacksmithing
combinations.label: Warrior guide recommendation
combinations.benefit: Mining gathers ore and stone for Blacksmithing. Blacksmithing makes weapons, mail and plate armor, and weapon stones; the Warrior guide specifically recommends this pairing for its weapon-stone benefit.
combinations.tradeoff: You spend time gathering and crafting, and a crafted upgrade is only useful when it compares well with current gear. Recipe materials and trainer/drop details are not recorded here.

combinations.name: Mining + Engineering
combinations.label: Sourced profession synergy
combinations.benefit: Mining supplies ore and stone used by Engineering. Engineering makes explosives, ammunition, scopes, goggles and utility gadgets; Forever also lists the Reagent Bot as a camp feature.
combinations.tradeoff: This pair focuses on gadgets and utility rather than Warrior armor. Engineering recipes may require specific recipes or workstations; detailed acquisition paths are not stored here.

combinations.name: Herbalism + Alchemy
combinations.label: Sourced gathering/crafting pairing
combinations.benefit: Herbalism gathers herbs used by Alchemy for potions, elixirs and other consumables.
combinations.tradeoff: This supports consumables rather than crafting Warrior weapons or armor; detailed Forever recipe lists and skill thresholds are not recorded here.

combinations.name: Mining + Skinning
combinations.label: Two-gatherer option
combinations.benefit: Both professions gather materials while questing. The Warrior guide recommends Skinning as an early vendor-gold option; gathered materials can be sold or saved for later.
combinations.tradeoff: There is no paired crafting profession, so you do not turn those materials into your own Blacksmithing or Engineering crafts with this combination.

secondaryProfessions.name: First Aid
secondaryProfessions.benefit: Makes bandages and Forever adds healing potions, poultices, tourniquets and disease remedies. The Warrior guide recommends First Aid to reduce downtime; secondary professions do not use either primary-profession slot.

secondaryProfessions.name: Cooking + Fishing
secondaryProfessions.benefit: Cooking makes food and Forever camp supplies; Fishing supplies fish used by Cooking. Both are secondary skills and do not compete for primary-profession slots.

activityNotes.before10: Learn the chosen primary professions from trainers and build profession skill separately from character level. Gathering skill rises from gathering; crafting skill rises by making relevant recipes.
activityNotes.before20: Check trainer rank gates as you level. Crafting Journeyman needs character level 10 and 50 profession skill; gathering Journeyman has no character-level gate but still needs 50 skill.
activityNotes.before25: Expert requires 125 profession skill; its character-level gate is 20 for crafting and 10 for gathering. At character level 25, Gathering Artisan can be trained with 200 skill; Crafting Artisan remains gated until level 35.
activityNotes.before35: Gathering Artisan is available from character level 25 with 200 skill. Crafting Artisan opens at character level 35 with 200 profession skill. Character-level gates and profession-skill requirements are separate checks.
activityNotes.artisan: At character level 35, the Artisan character-level gates for both gathering and crafting are met; each still requires 200 profession skill and the appropriate trainer rank. The rank raises the cap to 300.

Weapon upgrades matter greatly to melee damage.
The opening levels can feel slower before Stormstrike.

levelingRotation.title: Keep ready
items: Before level 30, use Rockbiter Weapon; from level 30, the leveling guide recommends Windfury Weapon.
Apply Lightning Shield between pulls.
Place only the totems useful for the next fight; totems stay where placed.

levelingRotation.title: During a pull
items: Use a low-rank Lightning Bolt to pull a distant enemy when helpful.
Use Stormstrike on cooldown once learned; respond to Improved Stormstrike resets once talented.
Use Earth Shock for damage or to interrupt a spellcaster.
Use Flame Shock on multiple enemies; use Frost Shock when threat is a concern.
Use Fire Nova when a Fire Totem is active and Mana allows; otherwise keep attacking.
Heal with Healing Wave after a pull and drink when Mana is low.

singleTargetRotation: Keep Magma Totem active; use Searing Totem when Mana is tight.
Use Rage of the Farseer when talented, for priority targets or a planned burst window.
Use Stormstrike on its six-second cycle.
Cast Lightning Bolt when Maelstrom Weapon reaches five stacks; avoid spending fewer stacks because it can reset the swing timer.
Use Earth Shock; use Fire Nova with a Fire Totem active when Mana permits.
aoeRotation: Keep a Fire Totem active and use Fire Nova on its cycle.
Use Rage of the Farseer when talented.
Use Stormstrike and Earth Shock between Fire Nova casts.
Spend Maelstrom Weapon at five stacks when talented.
AoE is Mana intensive; reduce optional casts when resources run low.
precombat: Use the recommended weapon imbue for your level/build.
For a group, the guide lists Strength of Earth, a Fire Totem, Mana Spring, and Windfury Totem as the baseline set; trade Magma for Searing if Mana is limited.
utility: Strength of Earth Totem for group Strength; Stoneskin Totem when physical defense matters.
Windfury Totem for groups; Grounding Totem against spellcasters.
Earthbind Totem for slowing nearby threats; Tremor Totem for Fear, Charm, and Sleep.
Totemic Recall can recover Mana when moving and replacing totems.
Healing Wave for efficient recovery between pulls.
levelingStats: Weapon DPS first; prefer a slow two-handed weapon (the guide suggests approximately 3.3–3.8 speed).
Intellect for Mana and talent scaling.
Strength for melee damage, especially before Intellect scaling improves.
Spirit becomes more useful for Mana sustain after Improved Stormstrike or Mindfulness.
Agility and Stamina are situational secondary choices.
endgameStats: Weapon DPS, Hit Chance, Expertise, Intellect, Strength, then Spell Power.

level60Builds.name: Standard Level 60 PvE
level60Builds.summary: Stormstrike and Improved Stormstrike form the core; the source also recommends Maelstrom Weapon, Rage of the Farseer, and Elemental picks including Elemental Devastation and Trial by Fire. Improved Ghost Wolf is optional; the source suggests two Tidal Focus points if skipped.
alternatives: Windfury Weapon is the source’s default imbue. Rockbiter may be preferable if Totem mechanics favor it; this remains unresolved in the source.
A Flametongue dagger setup is described as a possibility, not a verified recommendation.

level60Builds.name: Solo and small-group Level 60
level60Builds.summary: Trades deep Enhancement talents Maelstrom Weapon and Rage of the Farseer for more Mana sustain through Mindfulness while retaining Trial by Fire.
alternatives: The source frames this as an option when Judgement of Wisdom support is unreliable and Mana is a problem.
